claims.text: A combination of DFT and machine-learning algorithms calibrated with experimental data can determine melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The proposed computational approach can determine the enthalpy of fusion of high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The proposed computational approach can determine the entropy of fusion of high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The proposed computational approach can determine the volume change at melting of high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The proposed computational approach can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
Calibration using experiments on a subset of the high-entropy-alloy family allows predictions to generalize across the family.
Electronic structure and atomic arrangements are the structural mediators connecting the computational modeling to predicted thermodynamic properties.
Quantum-mechanical calculations and statistical learning provide the mechanism for predicting the thermodynamic properties.
Computational cost limits the applicability of the DFT-and-ML approach.
Experimental-data quality limits the applicability and accuracy of the DFT-and-ML approach.
The complexity of high-entropy alloys and limitations of computational methods create uncertainty in the predicted properties.
Validation should use high-entropy alloys that were not included in model calibration.
A deviation greater than 10% between predictions and experimental measurements is designated as ruling out the proposed approach.
